proposals.before: Murong Huang of Former Yan.
proposals.after: Murong Huang.
proposals.reason: Chinese is only 慕容皝; Former Yan is an editorial gloss.

proposals.before: In the beginning, Huang’s elder half-brother by a concubine, Jianwei Han, was fierce in arms and had heroic talent; plain was envied by Huang; younger brothers by the same mother, Ren the Campaign General and Zhao the Guangwu general, both had favor with Hui; Huang also was not even toward them.
proposals.after: In the beginning, Huang’s elder half-brother by a concubine, Jianwei Han, was fierce in arms and had heroic talent; he had long been envied by Huang; younger brothers by the same mother, Ren the Campaign General and Zhao the Guangwu general, both had favor with Hui; Huang also was not even toward them.
proposals.reason: 素 means heretofore, not plain.

proposals.before: Huang executed Zhao and sent agents to probe Ren, meeting him at the Xiandu defile.
proposals.after: Huang executed Zhao and sent envoys to probe whether Ren’s situation was genuine; they encountered Ren at Xiandu.
proposals.reason: The envoys met Ren, not Huang.

proposals.before: Huang sent his younger brother Jianwei You, marshal Tong Shou, and others to campaign against him.
proposals.after: Huang sent his younger brother Jianwu You, marshal Tong Shou, and others to campaign against him.
proposals.reason: Title is 建武, not 建威.

proposals.before: Ten days later Duan Lan and Murong Han (the kinsman who had joined Duan Liao) again besieged Liucheng; Huang sent Murong Han, who held the title of general who pacifies the distance, together with Feng Yi, to relieve the city.
proposals.after: Ten days later Duan Lan and Han again besieged Liucheng; Huang sent Ningyuan General Murong Han (慕容汗) together with Feng Yi and others to relieve the city.
proposals.reason: Besieger is 翰; relief general is 汗.

proposals.before: Early in Xiankang he sent Feng Yi against the Yuwen chieftain Sheyiyu and returned with rich spoils.
proposals.after: Early in Xiankang he sent Feng Yi against Sheyiyu of a separate Yuwen division and returned with rich spoils.
proposals.reason: Chinese 宇文別部涉奕於 names Sheyiyu as leader of a Yuwen detached division, not chieftain of the Yuwen as a whole.

proposals.before: Huang met them with fifty thousand foot and horse; both enemy columns fled from Liucheng.
proposals.after: Huang met them with fifty thousand foot and horse; Lan and Gui both fled when the army halted at Liucheng.
proposals.reason: Idiomatic English drops the named subjects 蘭、歸, replacing them with generic enemy columns.

proposals.before: Feng Yi urged that Huang’s duties outweighed his title, so in Xiankang 3 he assumed the kingship of Yan and proclaimed an amnesty.
proposals.after: Feng Yi and others, holding that Huang’s burden was heavy while his rank was light, urged him to style himself King of Yan; Huang thereupon in the third year of Xiankang illegitimately assumed the kingship and pardoned those within his borders.
proposals.reason: Omits 等 and the historian’s 僭 marking illegitimate assumption of the title.

proposals.before: He sent Murong Ke with two thousand horse in a dawn sally.
proposals.after: He sent his son Ke and others with two thousand horse in a dawn sally.
proposals.reason: Chinese 遣子恪等 marks Ke as Huang’s son and includes companions; the English name alone drops both.

proposals.before: The court promoted him to general who campaigns north, governor of Youzhou, concurrent Pingzhou, cavalier attendant-in-ordinary, with ten thousand extra households and unchanged barbarian titles.
proposals.after: The emperor again sent envoys to advance Huang as General Who Campaigns North, shepherd of You Province, concurrently governor of Ping Province, adding Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary and an increase of ten thousand households, with credentials, overall command, shanyu, and duke as before.
proposals.reason: The court and barbarian titles misrender 帝又遣使 and the specific titles 持節、都督、單于、公如故.

proposals.before: Murong Ping crushed Shi Cheng in western Liaodong, slew Huyan Huang and Zhang Zhi, and brought home a thousand captives.
proposals.after: Huang’s forward commander Murong Ping defeated Shi Hu’s generals Shi Cheng and others in Liaoxi, slew Huyan Huang and Zhang Zhi, and brought home more than a thousand households.
proposals.reason: Chinese 遼西 is Liaoxi, not Liaodong; the sentence also names Huang’s forward commander, Jilong’s generals, 石成等, and plundered households.

proposals.before: Huang’s forward commander Murong Ping defeated Jilong’s generals Shi Cheng and others in western Liaodong, beheaded their generals Huyan Huang, Zhang Zhi, plundered over a thousand households and returned.
proposals.after: Huang’s forward commander Murong Ping defeated Jilong’s generals Shi Cheng and others in Liaoxi, beheaded their generals Huyan Huang and Zhang Zhi, plundered over a thousand households and returned.
proposals.reason: Chinese 遼西 is Liaoxi (western Liao), not western Liaodong.

proposals.before: Huang opened Gao Zhen’s father’s tomb, carried off the coffin, the queen, treasures, and fifty thousand captives, fired the palaces, and razed Wandu.
proposals.after: Huang opened Gao Zhen’s father Li’s tomb, carried off the corpse together with Zhen’s mother, wife, and treasures, plundered more than fifty thousand men and women, fired the palaces, and razed Wandu.
proposals.reason: The Chinese names the father as 利 and pairs 其母妻 with the corpse; the idiomatic English drops Li and collapses mother and wife into “the queen.”

proposals.before: Next year Gao Zhen sent tribute and his father’s body was returned.
proposals.after: The next year Gao Zhen sent envoys declaring himself a subject of Huang, offered local products, and Huang then returned his father’s corpse.
proposals.reason: 稱臣于皝 is omitted, and the idiomatic English does not make clear that Huang returned the corpse after the submission.

proposals.before: Your Highness, with heroic and sage endowment, has been able to extend the former enterprise: south you crushed strong Zhao, east you destroyed Goguryeo, opened three thousand li of border and increased households by a hundred thousand, continuing the martial achievement of Murong Wu and Murong Guang, rivaling the great Earl of the West.
proposals.after: Your Highness, with heroic and sage endowment, has been able to extend the former enterprise: south you crushed strong Zhao, east you destroyed Goguryeo, opened three thousand li of border and increased households by a hundred thousand, continuing the martial work of expanding and broadening, rivaling the great Earl of the West.
proposals.reason: 繼武闡廣之功 is a verbal phrase of martial expansion, not two Murong personal names; the literal English invents Murong Wu and Murong Guang.

proposals.before: You have fulfilled the hope of a happy land; the people of China will welcome you with food. Who can compare with Shi Hu!
proposals.after: Recently you have deeply fulfilled the hope of a happy land; the people of China will all bring food to welcome you. Who then will remain with Shi Hu?
proposals.reason: 石季龍誰與居乎 asks who would still dwell with Shi Hu, not who can compare with him.

proposals.before: Even Wang Xian and Liu Ming, though punished, show my own lack of forbearance.
proposals.after: Wang Xian and Liu Ming, although their offenses would warrant ban and dismissal, also show my own lack of forbearance.
proposals.reason: Idiomatic English treats the pair as already punished; the Chinese only says their crimes ought to bring ban and dismissal, then restoration.

proposals.before: After Liucheng Duan Lan wanted to push on, but Murong Han feigned advice that spared Yan a deeper strike.
proposals.after: After the defeat at Liucheng, Duan Lan wanted to push on, but Murong Han feigned advice that spared Yan a deeper strike.
proposals.reason: The idiomatic rendering fuses the place Liucheng with the person Duan Lan, as if a single name.

proposals.before: When Duan Liao fell he fled north to Yuwen Gui.
proposals.after: When Duan Liao fled in defeat, Han again went north to Yuwen Gui.
proposals.reason: The Chinese subject of 北投 is 翰, not 遼; the idiomatic English makes Duan Liao the refugee to Yuwen Gui.

proposals.before: In the second year of Jianyuan, Huang followed to campaign against Yuwen Gui; on the line of battle was struck by a stray arrow; lay ill accumulated time.
proposals.after: In the second year of Jianyuan, he followed Huang to campaign against Yuwen Gui; on the line of battle he was struck by a stray arrow; he lay ill a long time.
proposals.reason: 從皝討 means Han followed Huang; the literal makes Huang the follower and leaves the wound without Han as subject.

proposals.before: At the time Xianbei Shanyu Duan Juan was Jin’s General of Agile Cavalry, Duke of western Liaodong; by nature loved men of talent, humbly extended invitation to Yu.
proposals.after: At the time Xianbei Shanyu Duan Juan was Jin’s General of Agile Cavalry and Duke of Liaoxi; by nature he loved men of talent and humbly invited Yu.
proposals.reason: 遼西公 is Duke of Liaoxi, not western Liaodong.

decisions.reason: s0002 is only the name 慕容皝; “of Former Yan” is not in the Chinese and is an editorial gloss, so the shorter “Murong Huang.” matches the source.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 慕容皝

decisions.reason: 素為皝所忌 means Han had long/always been resented by Huang; rendering 素 as “plain” is a mistranslation, and “he had long been envied by Huang” restores the adverb.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 素為皝所忌

decisions.reason: 遣使按檢仁之虛實，遇仁於險瀆 has the envoys, not Huang, meet Ren at 險瀆; 仁知事發，殺皝使 confirms they, not Huang, encountered him. The original dangling “meeting him” misattributes the subject.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 遣使按檢仁之虛實，遇仁於險瀆

decisions.reason: The title on You is 建武, not 建威 (Han’s title in s0011); “Jianwu You” corrects the literal mix-up.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 其弟建武幼

decisions.after: Ten-odd days later Duan Lan and Murong Han, the kinsman who had joined Duan Liao, again besieged Liucheng; Huang sent the Ningyuan general, a different Murong Han, together with Feng Yi and others to relieve the city.
decisions.reason: 蘭、翰復圍柳城 names the besieger 翰, while 皝遣甯遠慕容汗及封弈等救之 names a different man 汗. The proposal is right to split them and restore 甯遠 and 等, but its English still collides two homophones and inserts Chinese characters; 旬余 is “ten-odd days,” not “ten days.”

sourceWitness.excerpt: 蘭、翰復圍柳城，皝遣甯遠慕容汗及封弈等救之

decisions.reason: 宇文別部涉奕於 identifies Sheyiyu with a Yuwen detached division, not as chieftain of the Yuwen as a whole; the proposed phrasing matches 別部.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 襲宇文別部涉奕於

decisions.reason: 師次柳城，蘭、歸皆遁 names Lan and Gui and has Huang’s army halt at Liucheng before they flee; “both enemy columns fled from Liucheng” drops the names and misplaces the flight.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 師次柳城，蘭、歸皆遁

decisions.reason: 封弈等 records a group of advisers, 僭即王位 is the historian’s mark of illegitimate accession, and 赦其境內 is a pardon inside his borders; the original omits 等 and 僭 and flattens the amnesty.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 封弈等以皝任重位輕，宜稱燕王，皝於是以咸康三年僭即王位，赦其境內

decisions.reason: 遣子恪等 explicitly calls Ke Huang’s son and includes companions; “Murong Ke” alone drops both 子 and 等.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 遣子恪等率騎二千

decisions.reason: 帝又遣使 is the emperor sending envoys again, not a vague “court” promotion; 持節、都督、單于、公如故 are specific remaining titles, not “unchanged barbarian titles.”

sourceWitness.excerpt: 帝又遣使進皝為征北大將軍、幽州牧，領平州刺史，加散騎常侍，增邑萬戶，持節、都督、單于、公如故

decisions.reason: 遼西 is Liaoxi, not western Liaodong; 皝前軍帥, 季龍將石成等, and 掠千餘戶 are also in the Chinese and are omitted or altered (“captives”) in the original idiomatic sentence.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 皝前軍帥慕容評敗季龍將石成等於遼西，斬其將呼延晃、張支，掠千餘戶以歸

decisions.reason: The same 遼西 is the commandery Liaoxi, not “western Liaodong”; the proposed literal correction is accurate.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 敗季龍將石成等於遼西

decisions.reason: 釗父利墓 names the father 利; 載其屍並其母妻珍寶 is the corpse plus Zhen’s mother and wife, not a coffin and “the queen”; 掠男女五萬餘口 is more than fifty thousand men and women.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 皝掘釗父利墓，載其屍並其母妻珍寶，掠男女五萬餘口

decisions.reason: 釗遣使稱臣于皝，貢其方物，乃歸其父屍 records submission to Huang, tribute of local products, and Huang’s subsequent return of the corpse; the original drops 稱臣 and the agent of 歸.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 釗遣使稱臣于皝，貢其方物，乃歸其父屍

decisions.after: Your Highness, with heroic and sage endowment, has been able to extend the former enterprise: south you crushed strong Zhao, east you destroyed Goguryeo, opened three thousand li of border and increased households by a hundred thousand, continuing the merit of martial expansion, rivaling the great Earl of the West.
decisions.reason: 繼武闡廣之功 is a verbal phrase of continuing martial expansion, not personal names Murong Wu and Murong Guang. The proposal correctly rejects those inventions, but “martial work of expanding and broadening” is an awkward calque; “merit of martial expansion” is natural and faithful.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 繼武闡廣之功，有高西伯

decisions.reason: 石季龍誰與居乎 asks who would still dwell with Shi Hu once people bring food to welcome Huang, not who can compare with him; 邇者深副 and 皆將壺餐 are also restored.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 石季龍誰與居乎

decisions.reason: 雖其罪應禁黜 is hypothetical desert: their offenses would warrant ban and dismissal; s0127 then restores their offices. “Though punished” treats the penalty as already inflicted.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 雖其罪應禁黜

decisions.reason: 柳城之敗 is the defeat at Liucheng, followed by 段蘭 as a separate subject. Unpunctuated “After Liucheng Duan Lan” both drops 敗 and can be read as one name.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 柳城之敗，段蘭欲乘勝深入

decisions.reason: 及遼奔走，翰又北投宇文歸 has Liao’s flight as the circumstance and 翰 as the one who again went north to Yuwen Gui; the original makes Duan Liao the refugee.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 及遼奔走，翰又北投宇文歸

decisions.reason: 從皝討宇文歸 means Han followed Huang on the campaign; the original makes Huang the follower and leaves the stray arrow without Han as subject.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 從皝討宇文歸，臨陣為流矢所中

decisions.reason: 遼西公 is Duke of Liaoxi, the same 遼西 as elsewhere, not “western Liaodong.”

sourceWitness.excerpt: 遼西公

claimRetractions.reason: 妻 in 其母妻 is Zhen’s wife, not a queenly title; “the queen” exists only in the bad idiomatic English. The wife identification remains in c0451.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 其母妻珍寶
